proof_contract.api_controller: API server and controller starts remain projected through the independent runner dual-clock envelope and must precede the durable switch fence.
proof_contract.physical_gpu_start_claim: false unless a separately validated Triton-process dual-clock envelope is present; the current canonical runtime does not provide one.
proof_contract.pre_switch_terminal_fence: The exact 39 non-crossover bridge requests require Blue identity/result/digest plus committed and independently readback-visible durable effects whose causal sequences precede the switch fence.
proof_contract.prefix_actor_receipts: The exact four prefix requests times three actor stages remain committed and independently readback-visible in PostgreSQL before the switch fence. Triton receipt identity binds the raw trace, request nonce, trace ID, model/version/artifact and compute span.
proof_contract.triton_same_clock: InferRequest start <= model start <= compute start <= compute end <= model end <= InferRequest end on the Triton-local clock; no runner-clock projection is used for this nesting.

route_generation_contract.active_identity_change: Changing active model name, role, version, artifact, config, or output identity advances serving route revision even when weights are unchanged.
route_generation_contract.control_state_generation: C is a contiguous lifecycle/control fence and advances for every lifecycle mutation.
route_generation_contract.lease_fence_independence: GPU lease identity and fencing token are checked independently; route revision never substitutes for lease fencing.
route_generation_contract.non_route_actions: Load, drain, unload, lease takeover, and lease revoke preserve R unless they also change the active route identity or weights.
route_generation_contract.normal_request_binding: All post-switch normal requests bind the switch receipt new route revision E+1 even while Blue drain lifecycle actions advance C.
route_generation_contract.restart_aba: Append-only PostgreSQL route-revision history and independent readback preserve/reconstruct R across restart and reject ABA or reused route identities.
route_generation_contract.rollback_abort_second_rollout: Rollback and canary abort preserve or advance R according to whether the active route changes; a second rollout cannot reuse a prior route revision.
route_generation_contract.serving_route_revision: R is the C revision of the last route-changing action, may contain gaps, and is required to advance by exactly one only for each frozen E-to-E+1 switch.
route_generation_contract.terminal_binding: Runtime response, terminal record, durable effect entity/event/receipt, route-changing source row, and lease row carry exact R, model/version/artifact identity, transaction/readback identities, and canonical hashes.
